instructions:
Cavatelli alla Molisana

Molise-style cavatelli with slow pork-and-sausage ragù, tomato, red wine, and Pecorino.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/8 lb fresh cavatelli
1 7/16 lb mixed pork ribs and pork shoulder
2 fresh pork sausages
4 1/4 cups crushed peeled tomatoes
1 tbsp tomato paste
1 onion, thinly sliced
2 garlic cloves
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup dry red wine
1 tsp fine salt
3/4 cup finely grated Pecorino

For cooking the cavatelli
5 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a wide heavy-bottomed pot.

2. Add the onion and garlic and cook over medium-low heat for 5–6 minutes, until lightly golden.

3. Add the pork and brown for 8 minutes, turning the pieces on all sides.

4. Remove the sausage casings, crumble the sausage, and add it to the pot. Cook for another 5 minutes.

5. Pour in the red wine and cook for 3 minutes, until the sharp alcohol aroma has largely cooked away.

6. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, and salt.

7. Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook over low heat for about 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes.

8. When the pork is tender and the sauce is thick, transfer the larger pork pieces to a warm plate and keep covered.

9. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

10. Cook the fresh cavatelli until al dente.

11. Drain and transfer directly to the ragù. Toss over low heat for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and finish with the Pecorino. Serve the pork pieces separately or alongside the pasta.

Chef's note

Keep the ragù at a slow simmer so the pork and sausage season the tomato without reducing it too quickly.

instructions:
Sagne with White Beans

Rustic durum-wheat sagne with beans, tomato, and onion-carrot-celery soffritto.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the sagne
2 1/2 cups durum-wheat flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp warm water

For the sauce
1 cup cooked borlotti or white beans
1 2/3 cups chopped peeled tomatoes
2/3 cup tomato passata
1 cup plus 1 tbsp water

1/4 cup finely chopped white onion
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

For cooking the sagne
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup pasta cooking water to reserve

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on the work surface and add the salt.

2. Gradually add the warm water and knead for 10 minutes, until smooth.

3. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

4. Roll the dough to about 1/16 inch thick.

5. Cut first into strips 1 1/2–2 inches wide, then into rustic sagne pieces.

6. Arrange on a floured tray and rest for 20 minutes.

7. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

8. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 6 minutes.

9. Add the beans, peeled tomatoes, passata, water, and fine salt.

10. Cook over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, until the sauce reduces.

11. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

12. Cook the sagne until they float and are tender, about 4–6 minutes.

13. Reserve the pasta water, then drain.

14. Transfer the sagne to the sauce, add the reserved 1/4 cup pasta water, and toss for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Eggless sagne retain a rustic bite and absorb the bean-and-tomato sauce well during the brief final toss.

instructions:
Pasta and Beans with Mussels

Ditalini with cannellini beans, mussels, cherry tomatoes, garlic, chile, parsley, and crisp prosciutto.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 7/16 lb ditalini
3 cups cooked cannellini beans
1 3/4 lb fresh mussels
1 1/3 cups diced cherry tomatoes
about 7/16 lb prosciutto, diced
1 garlic clove, minced
1 small chile, finely chopped
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup warm water
2/3 tsp fine salt

For cooking the pasta
2 2/3 qt water
2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Clean the mussels thoroughly, removing the beards and shell buildup.

2. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a wide skillet. Add the mussels, cover, and cook for 4–5 minutes, removing them as they open.

3. Discard any mussels that remain closed.

4. Strain the mussel liquid carefully. Remove most of the mussels from their shells, leaving a few in the shell for serving.

5. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil and cook the ditalini until 3 minutes short of the package's stated cooking time.

6. Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

7. Add the garlic, chile, and half of the parsley and cook for 1 minute.

8. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes.

9. Combine the strained mussel liquid with warm water to make exactly 1 cup total. Add all 1 cup of liquid to the cannellini beans.

10. Drain the pasta and transfer it to the saucepan.

11. Finish cooking for 3 minutes, gradually adding the full 1/2 cup warm water while stirring continuously.

12. Add the mussels and heat for 1 minute.

13. In a dry nonstick skillet, cook the diced prosciutto for 3–4 minutes, until lightly crisp.

Service

Divide the pasta and beans among 4 bowls. Finish with mussels in their shells, crisp prosciutto, and the remaining parsley.

Chef's note

The strained mussel liquid directly seasons the beans and pasta, so the amount of additional salt is deliberately moderate.

title: Taccozze and Beans
instructions:
Taccozze and Beans

Molise-style taccozze with borlotti beans, pork rind, cherry tomatoes, onion, chile, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the taccozze
2 1/2 cups type 00 flour
2/3 cup water
2/3 tsp fine salt

For the sauce
1 1/4 cups dried borlotti beans
1/3 lb cleaned pork rind
1 onion, finely chopped
1 1/3 cups halved cherry tomatoes
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus 1 tbsp for finishing
1 chile
1 tsp fine salt

For soaking and cooking the beans
6 1/3 cups water for soaking
6 1/3 cups fresh water for cooking

Preparation

1. Rinse the borlotti and soak them in the cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and transfer the beans to a pot with the fresh water and pork rind.

3. Bring to a gentle boil and cook for 90 minutes, until the beans are tender and the pork rind is soft.

4. Add 2/3 teaspoon salt during the final 15 minutes. Reserve all of the broth.

5. Make the taccozze by combining the flour and salt. Add the water and knead for 10 minutes.

6. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

7. Roll the dough to about 1/16 inch thick and cut into irregular diamonds.

8. Heat 4 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan. Add the onion and chile and cook for 5 minutes.

9. Add the cherry tomatoes and remaining salt and cook for 5 minutes.

10. Add the beans, pork rind cut into pieces, and 3 cups plus 3 tablespoons of the bean broth.

11. Bring to a boil and add the taccozze.

12. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is done.

Service

Divide among 4 bowls and finish with the remaining 1 tablespoon raw olive oil.

Chef's note

The taccozze cook directly in the bean-and-pork-rind broth, allowing the pasta starch to thicken the soup naturally.

instructions:
Cavatelli with Ventricina

Handmade cavatelli with ventricina sausage ragù, tomato, bay leaf, and Caciocavallo.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the cavatelli
2 1/3 cups durum-wheat flour
3/4 cup warm water

1 1/4 cups tomato sauce
1/3 lb ventricina, cut into small pieces

1 bay leaf
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For cooking the cavatelli
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on the work surface and add the salt.

2. Gradually add the warm water and knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

3. Cover with a damp kitchen towel and rest for 20 minutes.

4. Divide the dough into small portions and roll into ropes about 3/8 inch thick.

5. Cut into pieces 3/4–1 inch long.

6. Drag each piece across the work surface with your index and middle fingers to create the characteristic hollow.

7. Arrange the cavatelli on a floured tray.

8. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan.

9. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.

10. Add the bay leaf and ventricina and cook for 4 minutes, until the ventricina begins to render its fat.

11. Add the tomato sauce, salt, and pepper.

12. Cover partially and cook over low heat for about 40 minutes.

13. Remove the bay leaf.

14. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

15. Cook the cavatelli for 7–10 minutes.

16. Drain and transfer to the ragù. Toss for 1 minute.

17. Turn off the heat and add the Caciocavallo.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Let the ventricina render some of its fat before the tomato is added so its spices and flavor spread evenly through the ragù.

instructions:
Lasagna Beneventana

Benevento-style lasagna with tomato sauce, tiny meatballs, Neapolitan salami, fiordilatte, hard-boiled eggs, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the tomato sauce
6 cups tomato passata
1 small yellow onion, finely chopped
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 cup water

For the tiny meatballs
2/3 lb ground beef
2 cups loosely packed stale bread pieces
1 cup water for soaking the bread
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 large egg
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil for browning
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For assembly
about 9/16 lb egg lasagna sheets
1 1/8 lb fiordilatte, cut into strips and thoroughly drained
about 7/16 lb Neapolitan salami, diced
1 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
4 large eggs
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Make the sauce. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan, add the onion, and cook for 6 minutes.

2. Add the passata, water, and salt. Cover partially and cook over low heat for about 1 hour.

3. Spread the fiordilatte over paper towels and let it drain.

4. Soak the stale bread in the water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it very dry.

5. Mix the bread, beef, Parmigiano, egg, parsley, salt, and pepper.

6. Form small meatballs about 5/8 inch in diameter.

7. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the meatballs in batches for 3–4 minutes. Drain and reserve.

8. Boil the 4 eggs for 9 minutes. Cool, peel, and crumble coarsely.

9. Dice the salami.

10. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

11. Spread a thin layer of sauce over the bottom of a roughly 8×12-inch baking dish.

12. Alternate lasagna sheets, sauce, meatballs, salami, fiordilatte, hard-boiled eggs, and Parmigiano to create about 6 layers.

13. Finish with pasta, sauce, Parmigiano, fiordilatte, and black pepper.

14. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

15. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Service

Cut into 6 portions and serve hot.

Chef's note

Drain the fiordilatte thoroughly before assembly so the lasagna does not release excess water during baking.

instructions:
Pasta alla Genovese

Neapolitan ziti with long-cooked golden-onion and beef sauce, white wine, celery, carrot, bay leaf, and grated cheese.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3/4 lb ziti
about 7 cups thinly sliced yellow onions
1 3/4 lb beef, cut into pieces
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1/2 cup finely chopped celery, plus a few celery leaves
1/2 cup finely chopped carrot
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 bay leaves
1/4 cup fresh parsley leaves
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
3/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano or Caciocavallo

For cooking the pasta
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Slice all of the onions very thinly.

2. Tie the celery leaves, parsley, and bay leaves into a small herb bundle.

3. Heat the olive oil in a very large pot over medium-low heat.

4. Add the celery, carrot, and onions and cook for 8 minutes.

5. Add the salt and herb bundle.

6. Add the beef and brown for 2 minutes.

7. Reduce the heat to very low, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and cook for 2 hours, stirring every 15–20 minutes.

8. Pour in the white wine and continue cooking for another hour, until the onions have completely broken down and the sauce is thick and hazelnut-brown.

9. Remove the herb bundle.

10. Remove the beef, shred it coarsely, and return about half to the sauce. Reserve the rest for serving.

11. Break the ziti into thirds.

12. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil and cook the ziti until al dente.

13. Drain and transfer the pasta to the onion sauce. Toss for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 4 plates. Finish with the remaining shredded beef, grated cheese, and black pepper.

Chef's note

Neapolitan Genovese is not a tomato sauce. Long cooking transforms the onions into a sweet, brown, creamy sauce that coats the pasta.

instructions:
Spaghetti with Clams

Neapolitan spaghetti with littleneck clams, garlic, white wine, parsley, extra-virgin olive oil, and chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

7/8 lb spaghetti
2 1/4 lb littleneck clams
2 unpeeled garlic cloves
3/4 cup dry white wine
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/4 tsp dried chile flakes, optional
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/2 tsp fine salt for the sauce

For purging the clams
2 1/8 qt cold water
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp sea salt

For cooking the pasta
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Soak the clams in the cold salted water for at least 2 hours. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

2. Heat the olive oil in a very wide skillet over medium heat.

3. Add the unpeeled garlic and chile and cook for 1 minute.

4. Add the clams and pour in the white wine.

5. Cover and cook over high heat for 4–5 minutes, removing the clams as they open. Discard any that remain closed.

6. Strain the liquid from the skillet carefully through a fine-mesh strainer.

7. Remove about two-thirds of the clams from their shells and leave the rest in the shell.

8. Return the strained liquid and shelled clams to the skillet. Remove the garlic.

9. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

10. Cook the spaghetti until 2 minutes short of the package's stated cooking time.

11. Drain and transfer directly to the clam liquid.

12. Finish cooking over high heat for 2 minutes, tossing continuously.

13. Add the clams in their shells, parsley, pepper, and fine salt only after tasting the sauce.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

The strained clam liquid is the core of the sauce. Taste it before adding salt so the finished dish does not become overly salty.

title: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
instructions:
Gnocchi alla Sorrentina

Sorrento-style potato gnocchi with tomato-basil sauce, mozzarella, and Parmigiano, broiled until bubbling.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the gnocchi
2 1/4 lb red or floury potatoes
2 1/2 cups type 00 flour, approximately
1 medium egg
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup fine durum-wheat semolina for dusting

For the sauce
2 1/2 cups tomato passata
1 garlic clove
6 fresh basil leaves
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt

For gratinating
about 1 3/4 cups well-drained diced mozzarella
3/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

For cooking the gnocchi
5 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Wash the potatoes and boil them in their skins for 30–40 minutes, until a fork passes easily through the center.

2. Meanwhile, make the sauce. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan, add the garlic, and cook for 1 minute.

3. Add the passata, salt, and basil. Cover partially and cook over medium-low heat for 30 minutes. Remove the garlic.

4. Drain the potatoes and pass them through a ricer while still hot directly onto the flour arranged in a mound.

5. Add the egg and salt and knead quickly, using only enough flour to make a soft dough that is no longer sticky.

6. Roll the dough into ropes about 3/4–1 inch thick and cut into pieces.

7. Ridge each gnocco on a gnocchi board or fork and arrange on a semolina-dusted tray.

8. Bring the cooking water and salt to a gentle boil.

9. Cook the gnocchi in 2–3 batches. Lift them out with a slotted spoon as soon as they float.

10. Toss each batch with almost all of the tomato sauce.

11. Spread the remaining sauce over the bottom of a baking dish and drizzle with the olive oil reserved for gratinating.

12. Add half of the gnocchi, half of the mozzarella, and half of the Parmigiano.

13. Add the remaining gnocchi, mozzarella, and Parmigiano.

14. Broil in an oven preheated to 480°F for about 5 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden.

Service

Serve immediately while very hot and stretchy.

Chef's note

Work the gnocchi dough quickly and use the minimum flour needed. Overworking the dough makes the gnocchi firm rather than tender.

Neapolitan Pasta and Potatoes with Provola

Mixed pasta with potatoes, sweet provola, tomato, soffritto, rosemary, and grated cheese.

2 cups plus 2 tbsp hot water
2 medium ripe tomatoes, diced

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat.

2. Add the carrot, onion, and celery and cook for 6 minutes.

3. Add the potatoes, tomatoes, rosemary, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.

4. Add 1 cup plus 1 tablespoon hot water, cover partially, and cook for 15–20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.

5. Remove the rosemary.

6. Lift out the carrot, onion, celery, about two-thirds of the potatoes, and 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.

7. Blend until smooth and reserve.

8. Add the pasta directly to the pot with the remaining potatoes.

9. Gradually add all of the remaining hot water while cooking the pasta, stirring often until al dente.

10. When the pasta is al dente, reduce the heat to very low.

11. Add the provola and the blended potato-and-vegetable cream.

12. Stir continuously until the provola is fully melted and the sauce is creamy.

13. Turn off the heat and add the grated cheese, black pepper, and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt.

Service

Rest for 2 minutes, then divide among 4 bowls and serve very hot.

Chef's note

The pasta cooks directly in the potato base, and its starch creates the characteristic thick, creamy texture. The finished dish should not be soupy.

title: Neapolitan Pasta and Beans
instructions:
Neapolitan Pasta and Beans

Mixed pasta with borlotti beans, pork rind, tomato, soffritto, bay leaf, and chile.

Yield: 6 servings

Preparation

1. Soak the beans in plenty of cold water for at least 8 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put them in a pot with the fresh water and bay leaf.

4. Bring to a gentle boil and cook for about 2 hours, until tender.

5. Keep the beans in their cooking liquid.

6. Heat the olive oil in a skillet and add the garlic, onion, and celery.

7. Cook for 6–8 minutes, until the vegetables are golden.

8. Add the pork rind and cook for 5 minutes.

9. Add the passata and tomato paste and cook for another 10 minutes.

10. Transfer the soffritto to the bean pot.

11. Add about half of the salt and enough bean cooking liquid to make roughly 5 cups of soup.

12. Bring to a boil and add the pasta.

13. Cook the pasta directly in the beans, stirring often, until al dente and very creamy.

14. Turn off the heat, add the chile, and add the remaining salt only after tasting.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve in soup bowls.

Chef's note

The pasta should cook directly in the beans. Its starch binds the broth and creates the thick consistency characteristic of the Neapolitan version.

9. Cook until the pasta is al dente and the sauce is creamy but not dry.

Add the broth gradually because the pasta cooks in the same liquid as the peas. Keeping the pasta starch in the dish creates the creamy texture.

Neapolitan Pasta and Lentils

Short pasta with lentils, potatoes, soffritto, garlic, bay leaf, parsley, and vegetable broth.

Preparation

2. Keep the broth hot.

3. Heat the olive oil in a large pot.

4. Add the onion, celery, carrot, garlic, and bay leaf and cook over medium-low heat for 7 minutes.

5. Add the lentils and potatoes and stir for 2 minutes.

6. Pour in 2 1/2 cups broth.

7. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, cover partially, and cook for 30–40 minutes, until the lentils are almost tender.

8. Add the pasta directly to the pot.

9. Cook until al dente, adding the remaining 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons broth in four equal additions, one every 2–3 minutes, stirring after each addition.

10. Remove the garlic and bay leaf.

11. Add the salt, pepper, and parsley.

12. Turn off the heat and rest for 3 minutes.

Service

Divide among 4–6 bowls and serve hot.

Chef's note

Pasta and lentils should be creamy and compact rather than soupy. The final rest allows the pasta and lentils to absorb the last of the liquid.

title: Ziti with Neapolitan Ragù
instructions:
Ziti with Neapolitan Ragù

Broken ziti with slow Neapolitan ragù of beef, pork ribs, sausage, and tomato, cooked for at least four hours.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3/4 lb ziti
1 1/2 lb beef short plate or brisket
about 3/4 lb pork ribs
about 3/4 lb pork sausage
6 cups tomato passata
2 1/2 cups finely chopped yellow onions
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 cup plus 2 tsp red wine
1 1/4 cups water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

For cooking the pasta
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a very large pot over low heat.

2. Add the onion and cook for 8–10 minutes, until soft.

3. Remove thick exterior fat and visible silverskin from the beef, then cut it into large pieces.

4. Add the beef, pork ribs, and whole sausages.

5. Brown the meats on all sides for 6–7 minutes.

6. Pour in the red wine and cook for 3 minutes.

7. Add the passata, water, and salt.

8. Bring just to a simmer.

9. Cook over very low heat for at least 4 hours with the lid slightly ajar, turning the meats every 30 minutes.

10. Stir the ragù every 20 minutes during the long simmer and keep the lid slightly ajar to limit evaporation.

11. Remove the meats from the sauce and keep warm for serving.

12. Break the ziti into pieces about 3–4 inches long.

13. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil and cook the ziti until al dente.

14. Drain and dress with generous ragù.

Service

Divide among 4 plates. Serve the ragù meats separately or alongside the pasta.

Chef's note

Neapolitan ragù should barely simmer for hours. Vigorous boiling reduces the sauce too quickly and toughens the meat.

Paccheri allo Scarpariello

title: Spaghetti alla Nerano
instructions:
Spaghetti alla Nerano

Amalfi Coast spaghetti with fried zucchini, Provolone del Monaco, basil, garlic, and black pepper.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2/3 lb spaghetti
6 medium zucchini, thinly sliced
1 1/2 cups finely grated Provolone del Monaco
3 cups plus 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for frying, plus 2 tbsp for finishing
1 garlic clove
20 fresh basil leaves
3/4 tsp fine salt

For cooking the pasta

1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Slice the zucchini into thin rounds about 1/8 inch thick.

2. Heat the frying oil to 340–350°F.

3. Fry the zucchini in batches until soft and only lightly golden.

4. Drain on paper towels and season with half of the torn basil and 1/4 teaspoon salt.

5. Finely grate the Provolone del Monaco.

6. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

7. Cook the spaghetti until 3 minutes short of the package's stated cooking time. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.

8. Heat the finishing olive oil in a wide skillet and add the garlic.

9. Cook for 1 minute, then remove the garlic.

10. Add the zucchini and 1/2 cup pasta water.

11. Transfer the spaghetti to the skillet and finish cooking over medium-low heat.

12. Add half of the Provolone and toss vigorously.

13. Gradually add the remaining pasta water and Provolone until a smooth cream coats the spaghetti.

14. Turn off the heat and add the remaining basil, black pepper, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Add the Provolone gradually over low heat with starchy pasta water. This creates the characteristic creamy sauce without separating the cheese.

Scialatielli with Seafood

Handmade Campanian scialatielli with clams, mussels, warty venus clams, langoustines, cherry tomatoes, garlic, and parsley.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the scialatielli
4 cups plus 2 tbsp soft-wheat flour
2 large eggs
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk
3 tbsp finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh basil
3/4 tsp fine salt

2 1/4 lb mixed clams, mussels, and warty venus clams

For purging the clams

For cooking the pasta
5 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Soak the regular clams and warty venus clams separately in cold salted water for 2 hours. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

2. Scrub and debeard the mussels.

3. Cut along the backs of the langoustines and remove the intestinal veins.

4. Make the pasta. Combine the flour, eggs, Parmigiano, basil, milk, and salt.

5. Knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

6. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

7. Roll the dough to 1/8–5/32 inch thick.

8. Cut into short, wide strips similar to thick tagliatelle.

9. Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and sauté the garlic for 1 minute.

10. Add the shellfish and langoustines, cover, and cook over high heat until the shells open, about 4–5 minutes. Discard any shellfish that remain closed.

11. Add the cherry tomatoes, half of the parsley, and fine salt and cook for 2 minutes.

12. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

13. Cook the scialatielli until they float and are al dente, about 4–6 minutes.

14. Drain and transfer to the seafood.

15. Toss over medium heat for 2 minutes.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and finish with the remaining parsley.

Chef's note

Scialatielli are intentionally thicker than ordinary tagliatelle and should retain a firm bite when tossed with the seafood.

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a very large pot over medium-high heat.

2. Add the beef, pork, and lamb and brown vigorously for about 30 minutes, turning frequently.

3. Pour in the white wine and cook for 4 minutes.

4. Add all three onions, carrots, celery, and salt.

5. Cook over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often.

6. Add the cherry tomatoes, crushed peppercorns, and Neapolitan salami.

7. Reduce the heat to very low and cook slowly for 2–3 hours, stirring every 20 minutes, until the meats are tender and the onions have collapsed into a thick cream.

8. Remove the meats, chop or shred some, and return that portion to the sauce. Keep the remainder warm for serving.

9. Break the candele into pieces about 3–4 inches long.

10. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

11. Cook the candele until al dente.

12. Drain and toss in the Genovese for 1 minute.

Chef's note

Using three onion varieties creates an especially complex Genovese. Long cooking should reduce them to a cream without the need for blending.

Melt the lard slowly until it becomes part of the sauce base; it should not fry or become firm.

instructions:
Maccaronara di Montemarano

Handmade Irpinian maccaronara with pork-rib, sausage, onion, and tomato ragù.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the maccaronara
2 1/2 cups durum-wheat semolina

For cooking the pasta

1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Make the ragù. Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the pork ribs and sausages for 3 minutes. Drain thoroughly.

2. Heat the olive oil in a large pot.

3. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes, until golden.

4. Add the passata and bring to a boil.

5. Add the ribs and sausages, season with salt, and reduce the heat.

6. Cook for about 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.

7. Make the pasta. Combine the semolina and salt.

8. Gradually add the water and knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and uniform.

9. Divide the dough in half.

10. Flour the work surface and roll each half to about 3/16 inch thick.

11. Roll the traditional grooved maccaronara rolling pin over the sheet with even pressure.

12. Separate the strips one by one and arrange them on a floured cloth.

13. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

14. Cook the maccaronara for a few minutes, about 4–6 minutes, until cooked but still firm.

15. Drain and immediately dress with the ragù.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve the ribs and sausages alongside the pasta or as a second course.

Chef's note

Maccaronara is thick and rustic. Its grooved rolling pin creates long squared strands that hold the ragù well.

Ravioli Capresi

Capri ravioli with hot-water pasta dough, aged Sorrento caciotta, Parmigiano, eggs, and marjoram, served with fresh tomato sauce.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 00 flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp boiling water
2 tbsp olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt

3 cups grated aged Sorrento caciotta

Preparation

1. Make the sauce. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan, add the garlic, and cook for 1 minute.

2. Add the tomatoes and salt and cook over medium-low heat for 20 minutes.

3. Add half of the basil during the final 2 minutes and remove the garlic.

4. Make the dough. Mound the flour on the work surface and add the salt.

5. Add the olive oil and gradually pour the boiling water into the center.

6. Mix first with a spoon, then knead as soon as the temperature allows, until firm and smooth.

7. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

8. Make the filling by combining the caciotta, Parmigiano, eggs, and marjoram until uniform.

9. Divide the dough into four pieces.

10. Roll one piece at a time to about 1/32–1/16 inch thick.

11. Place teaspoonfuls of filling over one half of the sheet about 2 inches apart.

12. Cover with the other half, press out the air, and seal firmly around each mound.

13. Cut 1 1/2–2-inch ravioli with a glass or cutter.

14. Repeat with the remaining dough.

15. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

16. Cook the ravioli in batches for 4–6 minutes.

17. Lift out with a slotted spoon.

Service

Dress with the fresh tomato sauce, Parmigiano, and remaining basil.

Chef's note

Boiling water makes the eggless dough elastic. The strongly flavored cheese filling needs no additional salt.

Sartù di Riso

Neapolitan baked rice timballo with ragù, ground meat, peas, provola, Neapolitan salami, hard-boiled eggs, and cheese.

3 tbsp butter, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Make the ragù. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

2. Add the celery, onion, and carrots and cook for 8 minutes.

3. Add the ground meat and brown for 5–6 minutes.

4. Add the passata, peeled tomatoes, 1 teaspoon salt, and half of the pepper.

5. Cover partially and cook for at least 30 minutes.

6. Keep the broth or water very hot.

7. In another pot, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and toast the rice for 2 minutes.

8. Pour in the white wine and cook for 2 minutes.

9. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons hot broth and cook the rice for 6–7 minutes.

10. Add the rice to the ragù and finish cooking with the remaining 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons broth in four equal additions; add the remaining 1/3 teaspoon salt with the final addition.

11. Add the peas during the final 5 minutes.

12. Turn off the heat and fold in about 3/4 cup grated cheese.

13. Cool for 10 minutes.

14. Add the salami, provola, and hard-boiled eggs and fold gently.

15. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

16. Grease a tall timballo mold generously with 2 tablespoons butter and coat it with about 1/3 cup breadcrumbs.

17. Fill with the rice mixture, pressing lightly to remove large air pockets.

18. Cover the surface with the remaining breadcrumbs and grated cheese.

19. Dot with the remaining 1 tablespoon butter.

20. Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until a golden crust forms.

21. Rest for 15 minutes before unmolding.

Service

Invert onto a serving platter and cut into 8 portions.

Chef's note

The rice should enter the mold soft and al dente. It finishes cooking in the oven and firms as it rests.

1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano
3/4 cup lard, divided
5 1/4 cups water
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Pour the water into a large pot.

2. Add about 9 tablespoons of the lard and the salt.

3. Bring to a boil.

4. Slowly stream in the cornmeal while whisking continuously.

5. Switch to a wooden spoon as the polenta thickens.

6. Cook over low heat for about 40 minutes, stirring very frequently.

7. Meanwhile, put the sausage and cracklings in a skillet and cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until well browned.

8. Add the black pepper and cool slightly.

9. Fold the sausage, cracklings, Pecorino, and Parmigiano into the hot polenta.

10. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

11. Grease a baking dish with the remaining 2 tablespoons lard.

12. Spoon the polenta into the dish and level the surface.

13. Bake for 50–60 minutes, until golden and firm on top.

14. Rest for 10 minutes.

Service

Cut into 8 portions and serve hot.

Chef's note

The polenta should be fully cooked and very thick before the meat and cheeses are folded in. Baking should firm it without drying it out.

Rest the filling for at least 12 hours so the flavors meld. Roll the pasta extremely thin so the finished tortellini remain delicate.

Preparation

1. Wash the chard and boil it for 5–7 minutes in a small amount of water.

2. Drain, cool, squeeze very dry, and chop finely.

3. Mix the ricotta, chard, egg, Parmigiano, salt, and nutmeg.

4. Cover the filling and refrigerate.

5. Make the pasta by kneading the flour and eggs for 10 minutes.

6. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

7. Roll the pasta as thin as possible and cut into strips about 4 inches wide.

8. Place walnut-size mounds of filling 1 1/2–2 inches apart.

9. Fold the pasta over, press out the air, and seal around the filling.

10. Cut rectangular tortelli with a fluted pastry wheel.

11. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

12. Cook the tortelli in batches for 4–5 minutes.

13. Melt the butter over low heat without browning.

14. Drain the tortelli well and arrange them in layers on a warm serving platter.

15. Season each layer with melted butter and Parmigiano.

Divide into 6 portions and serve immediately.

Chef's note

The chard and ricotta must be very dry. An overly moist filling makes the pasta difficult to seal and can cause the tortelli to open while cooking.

instructions:
Parma Anolini

Parma-style anolini filled with long-braised meat, breadcrumbs, Parmigiano, eggs, and nutmeg, served in broth.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta dough
5 cups flour
5 large eggs
1/3 tsp fine salt

For the braise and filling
1 1/2 lb beef or donkey meat
1 small fresh sausage, about 1/3 lb, optional
7 tbsp butter
1 onion, finely chopped
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1 tbsp tomato sauce

2 whole cloves

1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 1/2 cups dry breadcrumbs
1 1/2 cups finely grated aged Parmigiano Reggiano
3 large eggs
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg

For cooking and serving
3 1/4 qt beef-and-capon or beef-and-hen broth

Preparation

1. Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium-low heat.

2. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 8 minutes.

3. Add the meat, whole cloves, salt, and pepper.

4. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons broth, bringing the liquid almost to the top of the meat.

5. Cover and cook over very low heat for no less than 10 hours.

6. During the first 6 hours, add the measured red wine and 2 cups broth in four 1/2-cup additions, one every 90 minutes.

7. After 6–7 hours, dissolve the tomato sauce in the remaining 1/4 cup broth and add it to the braise.

8. At the end, remove the meat and mince it very finely.

9. Reserve the thick cooking juices.

10. Mix the meat and juices with the breadcrumbs, Parmigiano, eggs, and nutmeg until firm.

11. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

instructions:
Piacenza Anolini

Piacenza-style anolini filled with long-braised beef, breadcrumbs, Grana Padano, and Parmigiano Reggiano, cooked in traditional three-meat broth.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta dough
5 cups flour

1 1/3 lb beef for slow braising
2 garlic cloves
3 1/2 tbsp butter

Preparation

1. Insert the garlic into small slits in the braising beef.

2. Melt the butter in a heavy pot, add the onion, carrot, and celery, and cook for 6 minutes.

3. Add the beef, salt, and pepper and brown on all sides.

4. Pour in the red wine and cook for 3 minutes.

5. Add about 3/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon broth, cover partially, and cook over very low heat for at least 5 hours; after 2 hours add 3 tablespoons broth, and after 4 hours add the remaining 3 tablespoons.

6. Mince the cooked beef very finely.

7. Heat the concentrated braising juices and use them to moisten the breadcrumbs.

8. Mix the breadcrumbs, beef, cheeses, eggs, and nutmeg until compact.

9. Make the three-meat broth by putting the meats, vegetables, and cold water in a large pot. Bring slowly to a boil, skim, and simmer for 3 hours. Add the coarse salt during the final 30 minutes and strain.

10. Make the pasta by kneading the flour, eggs, yolk, salt, and the full 2 tablespoons water for 10–12 minutes.

11. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

12. Roll the pasta thin.

13. Place small balls of filling about 2–2 1/2 inches apart, fold the pasta over, press out the air, and seal.

14. Cut the anolini with a round cutter about 1 1/2 inches wide.

15. Bring the strained broth to a moderate boil and cook the anolini for 3–4 minutes.

Service

Serve immediately in broth with additional Grana or Parmigiano.

Chef's note

The filling should be dry and compact. The concentrated braising juices bind the breadcrumbs, beef, and cheese.

Dry-style Passatelli with Porcini and Truffle

Romagna passatelli served dry with porcini mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, onion, parsley, and fresh truffle.

Garganelli with Romagna Ragù

Handmade garganelli with Romagna-style veal, chicken-liver, prosciutto, Marsala, tomato, and Parmigiano ragù.

Yield: 4 servings

For the garganelli

For the ragù

Preparation

2. Roll the pasta thin and cut into squares about 2 inches wide.

3. Wrap each square diagonally around a small rod and roll it across a ridged comb.

10. Add the tomato and about 1 1/4 cups broth.

11. Cook over low heat for 1 hour; after 20 minutes add half of the remaining broth, and after 40 minutes add the final half.

12. In a separate skillet, melt the remaining butter and cook the prosciutto for 2 minutes.

13. Add the prosciutto to the ragù.

14. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

15. Cook the garganelli for 3–5 minutes.

Pisarei e Fasò

Piacenza-style breadcrumb-and-flour dumplings with borlotti beans, lard, soffritto, tomato, and Grana.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the pisarei
4 cups plus 2 tbsp flour
1 2/3 cups dry breadcrumbs
1 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp boiling water
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the sauce
1 1/2 cups dried borlotti beans

3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp tomato passata
3 cups plus 3 tbsp hot vegetable broth

1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Soak the borlotti beans for 12 hours, then drain and rinse.

2. Boil them in fresh water for about 45 minutes, until almost tender. Drain.

3. Put the breadcrumbs in a bowl and pour over 1 1/2 cups boiling water.

4. Cool for 5 minutes.

5. Add the flour and salt and knead in the remaining 1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons boiling water in two equal additions until soft and elastic.

6. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

7. Roll into ropes about 3/16 inch thick.

8. Cut into small pieces and press each with the side of your thumb to form a shell shape.

9. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a saucepan.

10. Add the onion, carrot, celery, parsley, and pounded lard and cook for 8 minutes.

11. Add the beans, passata, about 2 cups broth, salt, and pepper.

12. Cook over low heat for 30 minutes; after 10 minutes add 1/2 cup broth, and after 20 minutes add the remaining 1/2 cup broth.

13. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pisarei until they float, about 3–4 minutes.

14. Drain and transfer to the bean sauce.

15. Toss for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 6 plates and finish with Grana Padano.

Chef's note

Scalding the breadcrumbs before adding the flour gives pisarei their characteristic tender but resilient texture.

Preparation

2. Add the onion, carrot, celery, rosemary, bay leaves, and garlic and cook for 7 minutes.

3. Add the beef, salt, and pepper and brown on all sides.

4. Pour in the red wine and cook for 4 minutes.

5. Add the passata and about 1 cup broth.

13. Slide off carefully and arrange between two cloths.

14. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

15. Cook for about 20 minutes, checking the texture after 16 minutes.

16. Drain and dress only with the stracotto sauce.

The long hollow made by the needle lets the stracotto sauce enter the macaroni, so the pasta must remain intact during its long boiling time.

Strozzapreti with Romagna Ragù

title: Ferrara Macaroni Pasticcio
instructions:
Ferrara Macaroni Pasticcio

Ferrara sweet-crust pasticcio filled with macaroni, veal-and-beef ragù, mushroom béchamel, Parmigiano, and truffle butter.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the sweet pastry
3 3/4 cups flour
14 tbsp cold butter
1/2 cup sugar
2 egg yolks
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the ragù
about 7/16 lb ground veal
about 7/16 lb ground beef
1/3 cup dry white wine
5 1/2 tbsp truffle butter
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the béchamel
1 2/3 cups whole milk
1/2 cup heavy cream
2 tbsp type 00 or all-purpose flour
1 1/2 tbsp butter
1 cup loosely packed dried mushrooms, soaked, drained, and chopped
2 cups finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg

For the pasta
3/4 lb macaroni or sedanini

For the mold
1 tbsp butter
1 egg yolk for brushing

For cooking the pasta
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Make the ragù. Brown the veal and beef in a dry saucepan over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes.

2. Add the white wine and let it evaporate.

3. Cook for another 10 minutes, until the pan is nearly dry.

4. Add the salt and truffle butter, stir, and remove from the heat.

5. Make the béchamel. Melt the butter, add the flour, and cook for 1 minute.

6. Gradually whisk in the milk.

7. Cook until thickened.

8. Add the salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

9. Turn off the heat and stir in the mushrooms, cream, and Parmigiano.

10. Make the pastry by quickly working together the flour, butter, sugar, yolks, and salt until cohesive, without adding water.

11. Wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

12. Bring the pasta water and salt to a boil.

13. Cook the macaroni very al dente, about 3 minutes less than the package's stated time.

14. Drain and cool slightly.

15. Combine the pasta, ragù, and béchamel while all are lukewarm.

16. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

17. Butter a round baking dish about 12 inches wide.

18. Divide the pastry in two, roll the first disk, and line the bottom and sides.

19. Add the filling in a slight dome.

20. Cover with the second pastry disk and seal the edges firmly.

21. Decorate with scraps if desired and brush with egg yolk.

22. Bake for 30 minutes, until the crust is golden.

23. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Service

Cut into 8 portions and serve hot.

Chef's note

The contrast between the lightly sweet pastry and savory filling defines Ferrara pasticcio. The pasta, ragù, and béchamel should be lukewarm before assembly.

instructions:
Baked Bolognese Tortellini

Tortellini baked with Bolognese ragù, béchamel, provola, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 5 servings

Ingredients

For the ragù
1 1/8 lb ground beef
about 1/2 lb pancetta, diced
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp tomato passata
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp vegetable broth
1 cup dry white wine
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1 onion, finely chopped
1 1/4 tsp fine salt

about 2 cups diced provola or scamorza
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp béchamel
3/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 tbsp butter for the baking dish

Preparation

1. Put the pancetta in a cold nonstick skillet and cook over medium heat for 6–8 minutes.

2. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 8 minutes.

3. Transfer everything to a large pot, add the beef, and cook for about 20 minutes, until the liquid evaporates and the meat is well browned.

4. Pour in the white wine and cook for 3 minutes.

5. Add the passata, broth, and salt.

6. Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook over low heat for at least 4 hours, stirring every 30 minutes.

7. Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.

8. Cook the tortellini for about half their normal cooking time, around 2 minutes.

9. Drain and combine in a bowl with the ragù and béchamel.

10. Add the diced provola and fold gently.

11. Butter a baking dish and transfer in the tortellini.

12. Cover with Parmigiano.

13. Bake in a preheated 425°F oven for 15 minutes.

14. Broil for 2 minutes, until well browned on top.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and divide into 5 portions.

Chef's note

The tortellini should go into the oven very al dente because they finish cooking in the ragù and béchamel.

Rice with Pumpkin

Parmigiano Risotto

Carnaroli risotto with meat broth, butter, and Parmigiano Reggiano.

instructions:
Tagliolini with Prosciutto and Lemon

1. Mound the flour on the work surface, add the eggs, and knead for 10 minutes.

2. Form a ball, seal in a food-storage bag with the air pressed out, and rest for 30 minutes.

3. Roll with a rolling pin to less than 1/32 inch thick.

4. Let the sheet dry for another 30 minutes.

5. Fold gently and cut into thin tagliolini.

6. Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.

7. Add the lemon zest and cook for 1 minute.

8. Add the prosciutto and cook for 1–2 minutes.

9. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

11. Reserve the pasta water and drain.

12. Transfer the pasta to the skillet and add 1/4 cup pasta water.

13. Toss for 30–60 seconds.

Spoja Lorda

2. Knead for 10 minutes, until firm and smooth.

4. Mix the Raviggiolo, Parmigiano, egg, salt, nutmeg, and optional lemon zest.

5. Refrigerate the filling for 20 minutes.

6. Roll both pieces of dough into equal, very thin sheets.

7. Spread the filling in a thin, even layer over one sheet.

8. Cover with the second sheet and press gently to adhere.

9. Cut into 3/8–3/4-inch squares with a fluted pastry wheel.

10. Arrange on clean floured towels.

11. Bring the broth to a moderate boil.

12. Cook until the squares float, about 2–3 minutes.

Risotto alla Milanese

2. Steep the saffron in 1/2 cup hot broth for 10 minutes.

3. Melt half of the butter with the marrow in a saucepan.

4. Add the shallot and cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes without browning.

5. Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes.

6. Pour in the white wine and cook until almost completely evaporated.

7. Add hot broth one ladle at a time, stirring often.

8. Halfway through cooking, add the saffron broth.

9. Continue for a total of 16–18 minutes, until the rice is al dente.

10. Season with salt.

11. Turn off the heat and add the remaining butter and Parmigiano.

12. Stir vigorously for 1 minute.

Chef's note

Add the saffron halfway through cooking, then finish off the heat with butter and Parmigiano to preserve aroma and creaminess.

instructions:
Risotto alla Monzese

Carnaroli risotto with Monza luganega sausage, thyme, butter, Parmigiano, and white wine.

Yield: 4 servings

about 1/2 lb luganega sausage

1. Keep the broth at a gentle simmer.

2. Divide the luganega in half.

3. Remove the casing from one half, crumble it, and brown quickly in the olive oil for 3–4 minutes.

5. Reserve both portions.

7. Add the shallot and cook for 5 minutes.

9. Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate.

10. Add the broth gradually, one ladle at a time.

12. Continue for a total of 16–18 minutes.

13. Turn off the heat and add the remaining butter and Parmigiano.

14. Stir vigorously and season with salt and pepper.

Service

Chef's note

The sausage goes in at two stages: one portion seasons the risotto while it cooks, while the other stays juicier for serving.

5. Cover with a clean kitchen towel placed between the pot and lid.

6. Cook for 15–20 minutes without continuous stirring.

9. Meanwhile, crumble the pork mixture.

11. Add the pork and its cooking fat to the rice.

12. Add the Grana gradually and mix thoroughly.

Riso alla pilota is not stirred into a creamy risotto texture. The rice should stay dry and separate before the pork is added.

5. Rest in a warm place for 15 minutes.

6. Meanwhile, remove the sausage casings.

9. Uncover the rice and gently separate the grains with a fork.

10. Add the sausage and its cooking fat.

The covered rest finishes cooking without turning the rice into a creamy risotto. The grains should remain distinct.

Polenta Uncia

Brescia Malfatti

4. Squeeze the spinach extremely dry and chop finely.

5. Mix the spinach, Bagoss, Grana, ricotta, breadcrumbs, eggs, nutmeg, and salt.

6. Rest the mixture for 15 minutes.

7. Form small balls, elongate them slightly, and press a shallow groove in the center with the side of a spoon.

8. Roll each malfatto in semolina and arrange on a tray.

9. Melt the butter with the sage over low heat for 5 minutes.

13. Coat gently for 1 minute.

Service

Preparation

1. Knead the ricotta, flour, eggs, yolks, and olive oil until smooth.

2. Wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour.

3. Cut the vegetables and meats into small pieces.

4. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan with the thyme, marjoram, rosemary, bay, and sage.

6. Add the meats and brown for 6–8 minutes.

7. Add the rice, spinach, and broth.

8. Cover and cook until the broth has almost completely evaporated.

9. Remove the herbs and process until uniform.

10. Add the Parmigiano, yolk, salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.

11. Roll the pasta very thin.

12. Place small portions of filling, cover with another sheet, pinch between the portions, and cut with a pasta wheel.

13. Melt the herb butter over low heat for 5 minutes and strain.

14. Simmer the Freisa with the bay leaf until reduced by about 30%.

15. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

16. Cook the agnolotti for about 2 minutes.

Dress with herb butter and finish with drops of Freisa reduction.

Chef's note

Cook the filling until the broth is almost gone. It should be flavorful and dry before it is enclosed in pasta.

Preparation

1. Make the broth by putting the beef, marrow bone, celery, carrot, onion, water, and salt in a pot.

2. Bring to a boil, skim, and cook for 1 hour.

3. Remove the bone and strain the broth.

4. Cut the beef and pork into cubes.

5. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet with the garlic and rosemary.

6. Add the meats, season with salt, and brown for 8–10 minutes.

7. Pour in the red wine, cover, and cook slowly until tender.

8. Mince the cooked meats finely and combine with their juices.

9. Cook the rice directly in the broth for about 20 minutes, until most of the liquid is absorbed.

10. Season the rice with the remaining butter and Parmigiano.

11. Mix the rice, meat, eggs, pepper, and nutmeg.

12. Make the pasta with the flour, eggs, Parmigiano, and salt.

13. Knead for 10 minutes and rest covered for 15 minutes.

14. Roll two thin pasta sheets.

15. Place the filling, cover with the second sheet, seal, and cut with a fluted wheel.

16. Boil the agnolotti in salted water for 3–4 minutes.

Service

Dress with roast juices and serve hot.

Chef's note

Cooking the rice in the broth lets it absorb the meat flavor before it becomes part of the filling.

Asti Agnolotti Gobbi

11. Roll the pasta extremely thin.

12. Place small mounds of filling about 1 inch apart.

13. Fold the pasta over, seal around the filling, and cut with a pasta wheel.

14. Arrange on semolina-dusted trays.

Paniscia Novarese

16. Season with salt and pepper.

Trofie with Pesto

Liguria-style trofie with basil, pine nuts, Parmigiano, Pecorino, and extra-virgin olive oil pesto.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

3/4 lb fresh trofie
25 fresh basil leaves
2 tbsp pine nuts
1 garlic clove
1/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1/4 cup finely grated Pecorino Sardo
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp coarse salt

For cooking
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp pasta cooking water to reserve

Preparation

1. Rinse the basil quickly and dry it completely.

2. Put a few leaves in a mortar with the coarse salt and crush them.

3. Gradually add the remaining leaves.

4. Add the pine nuts and pound to a paste.

5. Add the sliced garlic and continue pounding.

6. Work in the Parmigiano and Pecorino.

7. Drizzle in the olive oil while mixing until smooth and compact.

8. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

9. Cook the trofie until al dente.

10. Reserve the pasta water and use it to loosen the pesto slightly.

11. Drain the trofie.

12. Dress with the pesto away from direct heat.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Do not heat the pesto directly. Emulsify it with a little pasta water and combine it with the pasta away from the flame.

instructions:
Trenette with Pesto, Potatoes, and Green Beans

Liguria-style trenette with basil pesto, potatoes, and green beans.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

3/4 lb dry trenette
1 cup diced potato
1/2 cup chopped green beans

For the pesto
1 packed cup basil leaves
3 tbsp pine nuts
1 garlic clove
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp finely grated Grana
2 tbsp finely grated Pecorino Sardo
1/2 tsp coarse salt

For cooking
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup pasta cooking water to reserve

Preparation

1. Put the basil, pine nuts, garlic, and coarse salt in a mortar.

2. Pound to a paste.

3. Add the Grana and Pecorino.

4. Work in the olive oil gradually.

5. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

6. Add the potatoes and green beans.

7. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

8. Add the trenette and cook until al dente.

9. Reserve the pasta water.

10. Drain the pasta and vegetables together.

11. Loosen the pesto with 2–4 tablespoons pasta water.

12. Dress the trenette, potatoes, and green beans away from direct heat.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Cooking the potatoes and green beans in the pasta water keeps their starch and flavor integrated into the finished dish.

title: Pansoti with Walnut Sauce
instructions:
Pansoti with Walnut Sauce

Liguria-style pansoti filled with borage and ricotta, served with walnut, bread, milk, and Parmigiano sauce.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
3 1/3 cups type 00 flour
1 tbsp dry white wine
1/2 cup water
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 1 3/4 lb borage
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp ricotta
2 large eggs
1/2 garlic clove
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the walnut sauce
1 1/2 cups walnut halves
1/2 garlic clove
1 slice soft bread
1/2 cup whole milk
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 1/2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp fine salt

For cooking
5 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Combine the flour, salt, and wine.

2. Gradually add the water and knead for 10 minutes.

3. Wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

4. Clean the borage and cook it covered over low heat until wilted.

5. Drain, squeeze very dry, and chop with half a garlic clove.

6. Add the ricotta, eggs, Parmigiano, and salt.

7. Mix until fairly firm.

8. Roll the pasta thin and cut into squares about 2 inches wide.

9. Fill and close into pansoti.

10. Dry on a floured tray.

11. Blanch the walnuts for 5 minutes and peel them.

12. Soak the bread in the milk and squeeze dry.

13. Pound the walnuts, garlic, Parmigiano, and bread in a mortar.

14. Work in the softened butter, olive oil, and salt until creamy.

15. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

16. Cook the pansoti at a gentle boil for 4–5 minutes.

17. Lift out carefully with a slotted spoon.

Service

Dress directly with the walnut sauce, tossing gently until the pansoti are evenly coated.

Chef's note

Keep the walnut sauce creamy and uncooked. Do not boil it after pounding.

title: Mandilli de Saea with Pesto
instructions:
Mandilli de Saea with Pesto

Paper-thin Genoese pasta sheets with pesto, potatoes, green beans, and toasted pine nuts.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
1 2/3 cups type 00 flour
2 medium eggs
1/2 tsp fine salt
4 tsp water
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

For serving
1 1/4 cups pesto Genovese
2 medium potatoes, peeled and sliced
1/2 cup cooked green beans
1/4 cup pine nuts

For cooking
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on the work surface.

2. Put the eggs, olive oil, and salt in the center.

3. Knead while adding all 4 teaspoons of the measured water.

4. Form a smooth ball and rest covered for 30 minutes.

5. Divide the dough.

6. Roll with a pasta machine or rolling pin until almost transparent.

7. Cut into large squares and keep them separated on a kitchen towel.

8. Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet for 2–3 minutes.

9. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the green beans if they are not already cooked.

10. In another pot, place the sliced potatoes in cold water with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

11. Bring to a boil and season with salt.

12. Cook 4–5 mandilli at a time for a few minutes, about 2–3.

13. Lift out with a slotted spoon and keep warm with a little cooking water.

14. Combine the potatoes and green beans.

15. Dress gently with generous pesto.

Service

Arrange the mandilli on plates with the potatoes and green beans and finish with toasted pine nuts.

Chef's note

The pasta should be almost transparent and cooked in small batches to prevent the sheets from sticking or tearing.

title: Stamped Corzetti with Pine-nut Sauce
instructions:
Stamped Corzetti with Pine-nut Sauce

Liguria stamped corzetti with pine-nut, marjoram, Parmigiano, and cream sauce.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
4 cups plus 2 tbsp flour
2 egg yolks
1–1 1/4 cups water
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the sauce
2 cups pine nuts
1 large garlic clove
1 cup plus 1 tbsp heavy cream
1 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
1 1/2 tbsp butter
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 tbsp finely chopped fresh marjoram
2/3 tsp fine salt

For cooking
5 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Combine the flour and salt.

2. Add the egg yolks.

3. Gradually add the water and knead until elastic.

4. Knead for 10 minutes and rest for 30 minutes.

5. Roll the pasta to about 1/8 inch thick.

6. Cut rounds about 2 3/4 inches wide.

7. Press each round on both sides with a corzetti stamp.

8. Melt the butter in a skillet.

9. Toast the pine nuts for 3–4 minutes and cool.

10. Chop the pine nuts with the garlic and marjoram.

11. Add the Parmigiano, cream, olive oil, and salt.

12. Mix until smooth.

13. Bring the cooking water and salt to a boil.

14. Cook the corzetti for 4–6 minutes.

15. Drain and immediately dress with the pine-nut cream.

Service

Divide among 6 plates and serve hot.

Chef's note

The sauce should be creamy but loose enough to collect in the stamped pattern of the corzetti.
